elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "Sparkling may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "Garman may not assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations ... without the written consent of the other party"

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Sparkling's consent to an assignment by Garman shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "Garman may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Sparkling"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "Garman shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a change of control of Sparkling"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: Vendor side remains consent-gated: "Garman may not assign this Agreement ... without the written consent of the other party"; no notice mechanic

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Sparkling's consent to an assignment by Garman shall not be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: All six preferred atomic elements are expressly delivered: affiliate assignment, successor assignment (merger/acquisition/sale of substantially all assets), Vendor consent gate, reasonableness standard, competitor bar, and no Vendor termination on Customer change of control.
Fallback is separately incomplete (no Vendor successor-assignment-with-notice right), but the locked target is preferred and preferred is fully met, so this is irrelevant to acceptance.

Edits are surgical: one word-level replacement converting "Neither party" to "Garman" in (d), one concise insertion supplying the absent Customer-side rights, and a short cross-reference "(except as permitted by Section 20(d))" in 3(c) to prevent the use restriction from cutting across the new assignment right.

No new exceptions, no duplicated protection, no boilerplate, and untouched terms (waiver, independent contractor) remain effective; "the other party" in (d) now unambiguously means Sparkling, so no dangling mechanic is introduced.
